concept: Blocking sort memory limit and allowDiskUse
summary: Source-anchored research for Blocking sort memory limit and allowDiskUse. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The aggregation limits documentation says profiler and diagnostic log messages include a usedDisk indicator when an aggregation stage writes temporary files because of memory restrictions. This indicates that some stage spilled; it does not alone identify the sort stage. (low confidence)

Spill files consume storage for the pipeline execution's duration; on Atlas, temporary-file growth can trigger storage auto-scaling to a higher storage tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Spring Data MongoDB AggregationOptions.Builder starts with DiskUse.DEFAULT; isAllowDiskUseSet() distinguishes that from an explicit choice, and serialization adds allowDiskUse only when it is set. Calling Builder.allowDiskUse(boolean) supplies an explicit disk-use choice. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Use explain to check for a SORT stage when diagnosing a blocking sort. cursor.allowDiskUse() has no effect on sorts answered using an index or non-indexed sorts requiring less than 100 MB; merely returning a large result set does not establish that this option is useful. (high confidence)

Starting in MongoDB 6.0, allowDiskUseByDefault controls default spilling for stages exceeding 100 MB. With the parameter true, allowDiskUse:false prohibits spilling for an individual find or aggregate; with it false, allowDiskUse:true enables spilling for that command. The cursor documentation identifies true as the parameter default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A sort combined with limit(k) can retain only the best k results in memory; if the retained results exceed the sort memory threshold, the operation still needs permission to spill or it fails. (low confidence)

Atlas documentation says Free and Flex clusters do not support temporary-file writes and ignore allowDiskUse, behaving as if it were false. The same page separately lists a 32 MB in-memory sort limit for Free clusters; it does not establish that this numeric limit applies to Flex. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
The 100 MB aggregation restriction applies per stage, including an unindexed $sort, rather than being a single 100 MB budget for the entire pipeline. (high confidence)

For the general server behavior documented here, a non-index-supported blocking sort is subject to a 100 MB memory threshold; allowDiskUse permits eligible operations to write temporary files beyond it rather than simply raising the in-memory allowance. Deployment restrictions can override this behavior. (medium confidence)

Mongoose Query.allowDiskUse(v) sets the allowDiskUse query option; calling it without arguments sets true. Its documentation presents this as a workaround for QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed, while the server documentation scopes its effect to eligible large non-indexed sorts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

An in-memory storage engine does not by itself guarantee that aggregation temporary data stays in RAM. SERVER-36388 documents that the external sorter can spill despite the engine being in-memory; an independent user reported local-drive I/O with allowDiskUse:true on Percona In-Memory 5.0.22 after a $group aggregation failed without it. The user observation concerns $group and does not establish every current sort implementation. (medium confidence)
